message: No detected input validation: User-supplied predictor_list from the POST request is passed directly into SQL queries and pandas operations without any type, range, or schema validation.

No detected untrusted source handling: The code connects to a PostgreSQL database using credentials from environment variables but performs no integrity checks, checksum verification, or source authentication on the retrieved data.

No detected label flipping detection: The code fetches target labels from the database and uses them directly for training without any validation of label distributions, expected label sets, or label-noise detection.

No detected data poisoning defenses: The only data cleaning performed is dropna() to remove missing values; there is no outlier detection, statistical anomaly checking, or filtering of suspicious inputs to defend against data poisoning.

No detected model integrity verification: The code trains a RandomForestClassifier from scratch each time predict() is called and does not load any serialized/pretrained model weights, so there is no integrity verification (no hash check, signature, or pinned revision) applied to any model artifact.
No detected label distribution validation: No code checks class balance, validates expected label set, or detects anomalous samples before training begins.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no trigger detection, activation analysis, or gradient anomaly detection of any kind in the training loop.
No detected differential privacy: The code uses a standard scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier with no differential privacy library or DP-SGD mechanism applied.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness testing libraries or techniques (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD, etc.) are present anywhere in the code.

No detected metric tampering protection: Although a train/test split is used, there is no held-out set isolation enforcement, no hashing/signing of evaluation data, and only a single accuracy metric (rf.score) is computed with no additional independent metrics or integrity checks.
No detected input sanitization: The inference path passes user-supplied predictor lists directly to SQL queries and the model without any shape, range, type, or schema validation.
No detected output bounds checks: The Random Forest predictions and feature importances are returned without any NaN guards, probability sanity checks, or threshold validation.
No detected prompt injection defenses: The model is a Random Forest classifier, not an LLM, so prompt injection defenses are not applicable.
